Some research mentions similar instruments in Mesopotamia and Egypt five thousand years ago, but it is not yet confirmed that they are this instrument. Around 609, Aenantius Fortunatus already called it a British instrument; it had three strings at first and later six, and was bowed, possibly the oldest bowed string instrument and a forerunner of the violin. Wales had related instruments from at least Roman times; there are clear records from the eleventh century, similar images appear on the continent, and it was once widely popular. Afterwards in Wales it long stood second to the harp, and the three-string version was played by bardic musicians. Today there are reconstructions and a folk revival, and Cass Meurig released the album Crwth in 2004.

The crwth is a traditional Welsh bowed string instrument, a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 321.22. It is built as a simple soundbox with a flat, fretless fingerboard and six gut strings; two G strings do not cross the fingerboard and serve as a fixed drone, plucked by the left thumb, while the rest are bowed with a horsehair bow. When played, the lower end of the body rests against the chest and a neck strap supports it. In medieval Welsh noble music the six-string crwth stood beside the harp and the timpan drum under a strict system of examination; the three-string version was used by bards and was also widely known across Europe.
演奏時將琴下端抵住胸口，以繞頸背帶支撐。發聲以馬尾木弓拉動跨過指板的弦；另有兩根: To play, the lower end of the instrument is set against the chest and a strap around the neck supports it. It sounds when a wooden bow with horsehair draws across the strings that pass over the fingerboard; two further strings of fixed pitch run parallel to the fingerboard without crossing it and are plucked with the left thumb as a drone. For tuning, the highest string can first be tightened to just short of breaking and the others tuned by interval; a beginner should first master sounding all six strings together across the flat bridge, then practise combining the drone with the melody strings. The three-string version needs less technique and is easier to take up.
